supplied: A is the number of records in the group whose the value of the first rule that applies: if primary diagnosed disease (`Patient.Diagnosis`) matches the pattern '%SLE%' ... then identification of the patient (`Patient.ID`); otherwise 0 is not missing; B is the number of records in the group whose identification of the patient (`Patient.ID`) is not missing
difference: The gold query `COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' THEN T1.ID ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(T1.ID)` counts every row, because ELSE 0 is never NULL. Integer division then gives [[1]]. The submissions computed a real share: repeat 0 used `ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e.Diagnosis='SLE' ...)/COUNT(DISTINCT l.ID),2)` and returned 2.74; repeat 1 used DISTINCT patients with `Diagnosis = 'SLE'` and returned 26.03. The explicit runs copied the always-true count and returned 1.0.
question_gap: no — the question asks for the share of SLE patients, and the gold's ELSE 0 makes the result always 1, so neither the question nor the evidence leads to it; the explicit version only describes this flaw in the gold.
